conventions.convention: Smoothing means the single-state conditional law given all observations Y₁,…,Y_T. Kernels are everywhere defined versions; values on null observation sets need not be unique. The empty observation product at T=0 is a singleton.

The forward Kalman filter must have positive-definite innovation covariances, and every forecast covariance solved in the backward pass must be positive definite. Ordinary inverses are used; no singular-forecast pseudoinverse extension is claimed.
The backward gain is C_k=P_{k|k}F_{k+1}ᵀP_{k+1|k}^{−1}; the backward loop runs from T−1 through 0 and is empty for T=0.
AC is assumed, while initial, process, measurement, filtered, and smoothed Gaussian covariances may be positive semidefinite and singular.

load_bearing.statement: Under AC, the finite-horizon linear-Gaussian model, admissible Kalman filter, and P_{k+1|k}≻0, the displayed Gaussian Q_k is an everywhere probability kernel with V_k⪰0. It is a conditional law of X_k given (Y_{1:k},X_{k+1}) and also a version given (Y_{1:T},X_{k+1}).

Assume AC and the finite-horizon linear-Gaussian model with positive-semidefinite model covariances, positive-definite forward innovation covariances, and positive-definite one-step forecast covariances for 0≤k<T. For every 0≤k≤T, the RTS output N_{d_k}(m_{k|T}(y_{1:T}),P_{k|T}) is an everywhere-defined fixed-interval smoothing kernel, and P_{k|T}⪰0.

Given admissible forward Kalman output and positive-definite forecast covariances, initialize at the terminal filter and, for k=T−1,…,0, compute C_k by Cholesky row substitutions and update m_{k|T}=m_{k|k}+C_k(m_{k+1|T}−m_{k+1|k}) and P_{k|T}=P_{k|k}+C_k(P_{k+1|T}−P_{k+1|k})C_kᵀ. Return all smoothed pairs.

published_dependencies.used_for: Finite horizon, compatible matrix dimensions, independent Gaussian noises, and allowance for singular model covariances.
Gaussian laws with positive-semidefinite covariance, affine projection characterization, and the zero-covariance point mass.
Independence convention for Gaussian coordinates on the auxiliary product space.
Rectangle-generated product sigma-algebras and the empty-product convention.
Joint Gaussianity of independent stacks, including singular covariance blocks.
Independent-noise realization and identification with the ordered transition-observation kernel law used in the backward factorization.
Measurability of translated Gaussian kernels and backward kernel compositions.
Countable additivity of the measure obtained by integrating the smoothing kernel.
Extending equality of finite joint measures from rectangles.
The auxiliary product probability space carrying independent Gaussian vectors.
Existence and uniqueness of positive-diagonal Cholesky factors for the forecast solves.

seams_checked.note: The forward algorithm and exactness theorem supply Gaussian filtering versions with possibly singular state covariances under positive-definite innovations. The smoothing consumers preserve those hypotheses and explicitly add positive-definite forecast covariances.

The downstream page explicitly retains the positive-definite forecast requirement for ordinary RTS. Its data-assimilation definition uses the terminal-observation smoothing convention and preserves the null-history version caveat; it attributes general conditional-kernel existence to the separate state-space existence theorem.
